summary: Where I went from "the React guy" to owning whole products end to end. Most of my time here has gone into work for our client ROSHN, a real-estate developer in Saudi Arabia.

engagements.name: Tenant Experience Portal
engagements.summary: A bilingual English and Arabic portal where store tenants raise requests, read announcements and manage their stores, while the leasing team runs the show behind the scenes.
highlights: I own the frontend, from architecture calls to the last pixel of the right-to-left layout.
Built the whole sign-in experience: two-step login, password resets, roles, and single sign-on with Microsoft and ForgeRock. Getting three teams to agree on one login flow was the real boss fight.
Made testing a habit instead of a chore, so release days feel pleasantly boring.
Some screens had grown past a thousand lines and were getting hard to handle. That's what she said. I broke them into small, reusable pieces without changing a thing users could see.

engagements.name: ROSHN.com and the ROSHN Design System
engagements.summary: ROSHN's public website, plus the design system that keeps their different brands looking like one family.
highlights: Built the public site on Remix with Arabic and right-to-left support, accessibility and mobile-first layouts from day one.
Built the design system from scratch. When designers change a colour in Figma, every brand's website picks it up automatically, with no developer needed. The designers loved it.
Set up a form engine driven by the CMS, so new forms ship without a code change.

engagements.name: Align
engagements.summary: Our in-house tool for setting goals and running performance reviews.
highlights: Led the frontend and built a kit of reusable widgets, so new screens snapped together like Lego.
Built a Microsoft Teams bot to collect employee feedback, because nobody opens survey emails.

summary: My first full-time role, and a crash course in enterprise software.
highlights: Moved a legacy enterprise app onto React, one screen at a time.
Made every screen work on phones and tablets, which in enterprise land counts as a revolution.
Turned a maze of step-by-step wizards into one simple form. Fewer clicks, fewer sighs.

summary: Where I learned that shipping with a team beats coding alone.
highlights: Built a drag-and-drop Kanban board with live charts, alongside five other engineers.
Made progress bars and graphs that moved smoothly and looked good doing it.
